rendered: The clinical sepsis serum samples came from septic patients with confirmed E. coli infection, septic patients with confirmed E. faecium infection[1]. So the infections were caused by E. coli and E. faecium. The control group was healthy volunteers serving as the control[2]. Each serum sample was measured repeatedly under the same conditions. The LDA score plot showed separate, non-overlapping clusters for the infected and control serum groups (panel c of Fig. 5[3]).

source.caption: Fig. 5. Discrimination of bacteria in clinical samples. (a) Color responses of BA@L-HGNRs toward live and autoclaved bacteria for intra-species viability-state differentiation of E. coli and E. faecium. (b) LDA for the differentiation of seven bacteria in human serum matrix. (c) LDA for the differentiation of serum samples from septic patients infected with E. coli and E. faecium.
